At that time, there were rākṣasī women, the first named Lambā, the second named Vilambā, and the third named Kūṭadantī.
The fourth is named Flower Teeth; the fifth, Black Teeth; the sixth, Many Hairs; the seventh, Insatiable;
the eighth, Holder of Necklaces; the ninth, Gaurī; and the tenth, Robber of the Vital Essence of All Sentient Beings. These are the ten rākṣasīs.
Together with Kūṣmāṇḍī, her son, and their retinue, they all went to where the Buddha was and addressed him with one voice, saying:
"World-Honored One, we also wish to protect those who read, recite, receive, and uphold the Lotus Sutra, removing their misfortunes and afflictions.
If there should be anyone who seeks out the faults of the Dharma Master, we shall ensure they find no opportunity. Thereupon, before the Buddha, they spoke this incantation:
Itiri. Itimin (Mín). Itiri. Atiri. Itiri. Niri. Niri. Niri. Niri. Niri. Lohi. Lohi. Lohi. Lohi. Tohi. Tohi. Tohi. Tuhuhi (Lohi). Lohi.
It would be better for it to fall upon my head than to cause distress to the Dharma Master.

Whether it be a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a preta, a pūtana, a kumbhāṇḍa, a piśāca, a vetāla, a kaṭapūtana, an umaraka, an apasmāra, a yakṣapiśāca, or a human piśāca; or whether it be a feverish illness, lasting for one day, or two—
Whether for one day, or three days, or four days, or up to seven days;
whether it be a chronic fever, or in the form of a man, or in the form of a woman, or in the form of a boy, or in the form of a girl—even within dreams—do not cause further affliction.
Then, before the Buddha, he spoke these verses:
If anyone does not comply with my spell and disturbs the one who preaches the Dharma, their head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ariṣṭa* tree.

This shall be as the sin of killing one's father or mother, as the calamity of pressing oil, as the crime of deceiving others with false scales and measures, and as the offense of Devadatta in causing a schism in the Saṃgha.
"Those who offend this Dharma-master shall incur such calamities as these.

After the rākṣasīs had spoken these verses, they addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, we too shall personally protect those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice this sutra, causing them to attain peace and security, to be free from all decline and affliction, and to eliminate all [misfortunes]."

[Regarding] poisons: The Buddha told the rākṣasīs, "Excellent, excellent! If you can merely protect those who receive and uphold the name of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, their merit will be immeasurable;
how much more so for those who protect those who fully receive and uphold it, and who make offerings to the physical scrolls of the sutra?"
Flowers, incense, necklaces, powdered incense, ointments, and burning incense; banners, canopies, and musical performances;

and the lighting of various lamps—ghee lamps, oil lamps, lamps of various fragrant oils, ghee-māndārava-flower oil lamps, *campaka*-flower oil lamps, *vārṣika*-flower oil lamps, and *utpala*-flower oil lamps—those who offer hundreds of thousands of such kinds of offerings, Gaun.
"O Emperor, you and your retinue should protect such Dharma-preachers as these.
When this chapter on the dhāraṇī was being spoken, sixty-eight thousand people attained the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).

The purpose of explaining the meaning of this mantra is precisely for these beings. Since they have already transformed their hearts and faces, those who uphold this sutra need no longer harbor any anxieties.
As an ancient worthy said: "Last night was the heart of a yakṣa; this morning is the face of a bodhisattva."
The Bodhisattva and the yakṣa are not separated by even a single thread. Thus, when the Way of Kings flourishes, the defense is maintained at the four frontiers;
when the Way of the Buddha is perfected, the protection lies with the Māras and externalists. Lambā is also called "binding" (saṃyojana); Vilambā is also named "free from binding.
"Ning shangxia" (寧上下) is the speech addressed to the various ghosts as a solemn exhortation. Vidyādhara is translated here as...
The red-colored ghost; the *gandha*, here translated as the yellow-colored ghost; the *umaloka*, here translated as the bird-voiced ghost;
the *abhamara*, here translated as the blue-colored ghost. As for the ghosts of fever, they are of the same class as the ghosts of pestilence and malaria.
"If they descend upon men" refers to the forms of these ghosts. "Even in dreams, do not cause further affliction" means to cause them to [protect] that Dharma.
The Master [Dao]an perceived this in a dream as well. As for the branch of the *āli* tree falling to the ground and breaking into seven pieces:
this refers to two of the five heinous crimes (*pañcānantarya*), namely the killing of one's father and mother. Regarding the calamity of pressing oil:

in the West, they press oil by taking many flowers until they are rotten, and only then extracting the oil. Because there are an immense number of insects within the flowers, the karmic retribution for pressing oil is also severe.

Those who deceive with measures and weights—such as giving out small measures while taking in large ones, or giving out small scales while taking in large ones—commit grave offenses because they defraud the people of the world.
Devadatta’s schism of the Saṃgha is likewise one of the five heinous crimes (ānantarya).
If any ghosts should further offend a Dharma master who upholds this sutra, the sins and transgressions they incur will be exactly like those of these [beings].
Therefore, know that one who receives and upholds this sutra is not only protected by benevolent deities, but even malevolent ghosts can reform their hearts.
Thus, in the final age, those who uphold this sutra should do their utmost within themselves; even if they encounter wicked people, they need not feel fear. I—
[The Buddha] spoke as follows: "I shall personally protect [you]. The Buddha then spoke, offering praise:
"If you protect those who uphold even the name of this sutra, their merit is already immeasurable;
how much more so for those who protect and uphold the entire sutra, or even those who provide various offerings to this complete sutra—how could one possibly measure their merit? Sumati.
The "na-hua" (flower) is the *sumanā* flower; the "po-shi-jia" is the *pāriyātraka*; and the "you-po-luo" is the blue lotus (*utpala*).
It is said that one should take these various flowers as lamp oil to make offerings to the Buddha.
Below the name of Gautama, he calls out their names again and entrusts them, saying: "If you can protect, uphold, and make offerings to this sutra..."
O Custodians, not only will they be benefited, but the merit and blessings you yourselves shall obtain are likewise immeasurable.
Since both parties will have mutual benefit, you should protect such Dharma-preachers as these.
Having spoken thus, the great assembly attained benefit.
The twenty-seventh chapter, "The King of Sublime Adornment," states in verse:
Diseases have no root; do not speculate rashly. When the deviant wind strikes, disaster arises.
One need only take a single dose of *niuhuang-san* (cow bezoar powder), and all stubborn phlegm will be drawn out. This is the "Original Power of the Medicine King" (*Bhaiṣajyarāja-pūrvayoga*).
This chapter reveals the fundamental virtue of the Medicine King seeking the Dharma and making offerings to the Buddhas during his causal stage. This is the chapter [on the Medicine King].
Although this is titled "The Past Deeds of King Wonderful Adornment," it actually reveals the skillful means by which Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata deliver sentient beings.
In a former life as a bodhisattva, King Wonderful Adornment was once a bhikṣu who practiced the Way in the company of others.

One day, seeing the king’s royal procession, he suddenly gave rise to a lustful mind. Later, having become a king himself, he became greedily attached to the five desires and failed to revere the Three [Jewels].
O Jewel, due to the causes and conditions of his past cultivation of the Way, those two friends manifested as two sons to transform their deviant minds.

One must know that there are difficulties and ease in the transformation and deliverance of sentient beings: for instance, when Pu-xing (Never-Disparaging) transformed the fourfold assembly, they instead reviled and insulted him—this was a great waste of energy;
whereas when Wenshu (Mañjuśrī) transformed the dragon girl, it was like the two sons transforming Miaozhuangyan.
Yan, sudden faith at once—how could this be easy? It is because capacities vary in depth that there is ease or difficulty in being transformed by the teachings;
it does not mean that there is any superiority or inferiority in the skillful means of the Bodhisattvas.

At that time, the Buddha addressed the great assembly: "In the distant past, beyond immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom (*Meghadundubhisvararāja-puṣpajñāna*), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
His land was named Radiant Adornment (*Prabhāvyūha*), and his eon was named Joyful Sight (*Priyadarśana*). This was the Dharma of that Buddha."
In that land, there was a king named Wondrous Adornment (*Suśobhana*). His queen was named Pure Virtue (*Viśuddhaguṇā*). He had two sons:
the first was named Pure Treasury (*Viśuddhagarbha*), and the second was named Pure Eye (*Viśuddhanetra*). These two sons possessed great supernormal powers, merit, and wisdom;

they had long cultivated the path practiced by bodhisattvas, namely the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*), and the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*).

The perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditation, the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of skillful means,
loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, up to and including the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment— all these he fully understands and thoroughly penetrates.

Furthermore, he attained the Bodhisattva’s Pure Samādhi, the Sun and Constellation Samādhi, the Pure Light Samādhi, the Pure Color Samādhi, the Pure Illumination Samādhi, the Long Adornment Samādhi, and the Great Majestic Virtue Treasury Samādhi. Within these samādhis...
He also thoroughly mastered them all.
The Buddha’s name was Meghadundubhisvararāja-puṣpadhvaja-jñāna; the land was named Prabhāsa-vyūha; the eon was named Priyadarśana; the king was named Suvyūha;
his queen was named Viśuddhaguṇa. In the "Chapter on the Medicine King," the Medicine King was named Sarva... (omitted).
Sentient beings rejoice in seeing him. The Buddha’s name is Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī. He was born into the family of King Vimalaśrī.

In response to Śaradvatiputra’s question regarding the former life of Bhaiṣajyarāja, it is said that in the "Chapter on Gadgadasvara," the world is named Vimalaprabhālaṃkṛta and the Buddha is named Padmavimalacandrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña;
the bodhisattva is named Gadgadasvara. In the past, there was a Buddha named Meghadundubhisvararāja.
The name of the land was Manifesting All Worlds, and the name of the eon was Joyful Vision; these all constitute a single coherent narrative.

If spoken of in terms of worldly affairs, then King Wondrous Adornment was the sovereign, his consort was the internal support, and Pure Treasury and Pure Eye were the sons who upheld the family legacy.
If spoken of in terms of principle, King Wondrous Adornment is the Buddha-nature inherently possessed by sentient beings, and the consort is...
It is named Pure Virtue (*viśuddhaguṇa*). This refers to the immeasurable and inconceivable qualities of meaning inherently possessed by one's original nature.

The purity of the *ālayavijñāna* is called the "Pure Treasury" (*viśuddhagarbha*); the purity of the Dharma-eye is called the "Pure Eye" (*viśuddhacakṣus*). This means that the originally existing Buddha-nature is fully endowed with immeasurable inherent qualities;
therefore, it is adorned with sublime excellence. It is primordially sovereign and does not depend on cultivation for its accomplishment. Due to that sudden...

A single thought arises, and one subsequently gives rise to deluded attachment, thereby falling into false views. If one does not transform defilement into purity, one cannot attain wondrous adornment.
If the *ālayavijñāna* (storehouse consciousness) is not pure, one cannot attain wondrous adornment. If the Dharma-eye is not pure, one cannot attain wondrous adornment.
One must necessarily transform the *ālayavijñāna* and open the Dharma-eye; only when the myriad virtues are purified can the King of Wondrous Adornment exercise sovereign mastery.

There is no obstruction; this is the conclusion of this single sutra. Therefore, the *Śūraṅgama* is named "Sublime Adornment" (*Miao Zhuangyan*), and the *Avataṃsaka* is named "Sublime Array" (*Miaoyan*).
If one wishes to succeed to the throne of the Dharma King, it must be through such means that one can reach it;

thus, this is set forth here. From the second section below, the virtues of the two sons are revealed: they possess both the provisional and the real, and are fully proficient in both the Great and the Small Vehicles. Furthermore...
One attains the seven great samādhis. By transforming the defiled manas, one attains the pure samādhi.
By transforming the mind of greedy attachment, one attains the sun and constellations samādhi. By transforming the darkness of ignorance, one attains the pure light samādhi.
By transforming the dharma of form, one attains the Samādhi of Pure Form. Because wisdom is immeasurable, one attains the Samādhi of Pure Illumination.
Because merit is boundless, one attains the Samādhi of Long Adornment. Because majestic power is inexhaustible, one attains the Samādhi of the Treasury of Great Majestic Power.
These are all obtained by transforming the preceding seven consciousnesses.
At that time, that Buddha, wishing to guide King Subhavyūha and out of compassion for sentient beings, preached this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Then, the two sons, Viśuddhagarbha and Viśuddhanetra, went to their mother’s place, joined their palms with ten fingers together, and said:
"We pray that you, Mother, will go to the presence of the Buddha Meghadundubhisvararājasaṃkusumitābhijña; we, too, shall attend upon you."
They approached to make offerings and pay their respects. Why was this? Because this Buddha was preaching the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* amidst the assembly of devas and humans;

it was fitting that they should listen and receive it. Their mother said to her sons, "Your father believes in and accepts the teachings of non-Buddhists and is deeply attached to the Brahmanical dharma.
You should go and inform your father so that we may all go together. Then Viśuddhagarbha and Viśuddhanetra joined their ten fingers in homage.
They prostrated at their mother’s feet and said, "We are sons of the Dharma King, yet we have been born into this family of wrong views.
Their mother said to her sons, "You should take pity on your father and manifest spiritual transformations for him; if he sees them, his mind will surely become pure.
Alternatively, you may go with us to where the Buddha is. Thereupon, out of concern for their father, the two sons rose into the air to a height of seven [yojanas].

The Tāla tree manifested various supernatural transformations in mid-air: walking, standing, sitting, and reclining; water flowed from the upper part of its body while fire issued from its lower part;
water flowed from the lower part of its body while fire issued from its upper part; or it manifested a massive body that filled the entirety of space.
Furthermore, he manifested smallness and again manifested largeness; he vanished from mid-air and suddenly appeared upon the ground;

he entered the earth as if it were water and walked upon water as if it were solid ground. He displayed such various supernormal transformations that his father, the king, attained pure faith and understanding.
At that time, the father saw his sons’ supernatural powers were such as this; his heart was filled with great joy, having attained what he had never experienced before.
Joining his palms toward his sons, he said: "Who is your teacher? Whose disciples are you? The two sons replied:
"Great King, that Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Wisdom is currently seated upon the Dharma throne beneath a Bodhi tree made of the seven precious gems. At that moment—
"Among all the multitudes of devas and humans in the world, he who extensively preaches the Lotus Sutra is our teacher; we are his disciples.
The father said to his sons, "I now also wish to see your teacher. We should go together to pay him homage."
The Dharma King wishes to lead the King of Men into the Mahāyāna; therefore, he preaches the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* as an incitement.
This is what is meant by "the Buddha-seed arises from conditions," and for this reason, he speaks of the Mahāyāna. Regarding the passage "At that time, Śuddhodana... and so forth:

the reason he exhorts his mother to listen to the Dharma, desiring to convert his father but first urging his mother to go to the Buddha, is because he wishes his mother to initiate the process, gradually perfuming and gently guiding him.
The mother spoke as follows, instructing her son to exhort his father: "The Brahmin’s pride is exceedingly high.
Since your father has already accepted this teaching of false views, you should not fail to urge him to go to the Buddha, instead of urging me."
"If you wish for me to hear the Dharma, you must urge your father to go along.

This was because his mother knew in advance that her husband deeply believed in non-Buddhist paths and would not be willing to visit the Buddha; thus, she exhorted her son to lead him there. [End of] Jingzang.
The two sons were distressed and said, "We, mother and sons, have deep faith in the Buddha-dharma;
we are all children of the Dharma King, endowed with right knowledge and vision. Why have we been born into a family of such false views? The mother told them to go down and convert their father.
"When it is said that you should feel anxiety for your father, it means that your father has entered into heterodoxy; this is what you two sons should keep in mind as your concern.
'To manifest supernatural transformations' refers to demonstrating the method for converting your father. For those with false views—"
Not understanding the True Dharma, he would certainly not permit us to go to the Buddha, nor would he allow us to leave the household life.
Unless a supernatural manifestation were displayed, it would be impossible to move his heart and change his resolve;

therefore, the two sons manifested spiritual transformations to turn his perverse mind, and only then did they lead him to listen to the Dharma. Thereupon, the two sons manifested their supernormal powers. [The father’s] wrong views—
This place is the ground of manifesting supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*). If one is free from false views, even if one possesses supernatural powers, there is nothing to be bestowed.

At that time, the father descended [from his seat], and seeing the supernatural powers, he was filled with joy. His roots of goodness from past lives sprang up vibrantly; therefore, he honored his son and subsequently inquired about his teacher.
From "The two sons" onwards, [the text] respectfully sets forth the teacher’s Dharma. Having already transformed [them] through miraculous manifestations...
His mind desired to wash away its defilements with the water of the Dharma; thus, he set forth his teacher’s instructions to entice him to go to the Buddha.
As for the father’s words below, the son’s heart delighted in beholding the Buddha—this is what is meant by a person of sharp faculties who turns at a single stroke.
Thereupon, the two sons descended from the air and approached their mother. With palms joined, they said to her: "The Father King has now attained faith and understanding;
he is capable of giving rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. We have performed the work of a Buddha for our father’s sake.
We pray that you will grant us permission to leave the household life and practice the Way under that Buddha. At that time, the two sons, wishing to...
To restate their intention, they addressed their mother in verse:
"We pray that you will release us so that we may leave the household life and become śramaṇas. Buddhas are extremely difficult to encounter; we shall follow and train under the Buddha."

It is as rare as the *utpala* flower; even rarer than that is to encounter a Buddha, and even more difficult is to be liberated from all calamities. "I pray that you will grant me permission to leave the household life.
His mother then replied, "I grant you permission to leave the household life. Why is this? Because a Buddha is difficult to encounter. Thereupon, the two sons—
He said to his parents, “Excellent, my parents! I pray that you will go at once to the presence of the Buddha Cloud-Resounding Sound King Flower-Wisdom to attend upon and make offerings to him.
Why is this? A Buddha is difficult to encounter, like the udumbara flower, or like a one-eyed turtle encountering the hole of a floating log.
Yet we, through the profound depth of our past merit, have been born into the presence of the Buddha’s Dharma.”
Therefore, parents, you should grant us permission to leave the household life. Why is this? Because Buddhas are difficult to encounter, and such a time is likewise hard to find.
At that time, the eighty-four thousand women of King Subhavyūha’s inner palace were all capable of receiving and upholding this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
The Bodhisattva Viśuddhanetra had long since attained mastery in the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Samādhi*.
The Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha had, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, attained mastery in the samādhi of being free from all evil destinies;
desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave behind all evil destinies, he acted accordingly.

The king’s consort had attained the samādhi of the assembly of all Buddhas and was able to know the secret treasury of all Buddhas. In this way, through the power of skillful means, the two sons skillfully transformed [the people].
His father caused his mind to develop faith and understanding, and he came to delight in the Buddha-dharma. Thereupon, King Zhuāngmiàoyán, together with his ministers and retinue;
Lady Jìngdé, together with the ladies of the inner palace and their retinue; and the king’s two sons, together with forty-two thousand people, all went at once to the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, they bowed their heads at his feet and circumambulated the Buddha three times.
[They] circumambulated [the Buddha] and then stood to one side. At that time, the Buddha preached the Dharma for the king, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him;
the king was greatly delighted. As for the two sons covering their mother and descending from the sky: when they manifested these supernormal transformations, their bodies were in the void.
Having finished transforming their father, they then addressed their mother; thus, they descended from the sky. "Now, having attained faith and understanding" refers to the father of the past.
"He did not believe in the Buddha-dharma, yet now that he has witnessed this supernatural manifestation, his former resolve has risen up once more.
You who are capable of giving rise to the bodhicitta—our father the King is currently in a state of profound and firm faith;
this is precisely the time to go to the Buddha to hear the Dharma and clarify this great matter. Do not let it pass you by. Since we have already persuaded our father..."
With a mind of resolve, his task was completed; thus he wished for his mother to go to the Buddha and leave the household life.
In the verse, the character *fang* (放) is read with the rising tone (*shǎngshēng*), meaning "to emulate. This refers to emulating us by also leaving the household life.

He first addressed his mother because he knew that her karmic conditions had long since matured. His mother then consented; mother and son were in perfect accord, and she granted him permission to leave the household life. At that—
This is the lower [section]. It exhorts them to hasten their journey; because his mother permitted his renunciation, he also exhorted his father to listen to the Dharma.
As for the words "I pray that you go at this time," it means that at this very moment King Meghadundubhisvara is preaching the Lotus Sutra;
one should quickly go to the Buddha’s abode to make offerings and draw near to him, and must not remain lingering. We have planted roots of merit deeply in past kalpas.
"Since we have encountered the Buddha-dharma in this life, you should grant us permission to leave the household life. For Buddhas are difficult to meet and the right time is likewise hard to find;
therefore, we must behold the Buddha while there is still time, lest we let these precious moments go to waste. At that point, [the text] clearly reveals how past conditions had matured:
every member of the single family was a kinsman of Bodhi, as expressed in the verse: "The whole family gathered together in one place."
They spoke together of the discourse on non-arising. Because they opened the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, they attained the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi*.
Because they relinquished the *ālayavijñāna*, they attained the *Dūrībhāvāpāyika-samādhi*. Because they knew the secret treasury of the Tathāgata, they attained the *Puṇyasamuccaya-rāja-samādhi*.
Regarding the "two sons" below, this explains the teaching of skillful means; it is said that there are two sons who serve as the predominant conditions (*adhipati*).
Regarding the conditions: although King Subhavyūha wished to believe in heterodox teachings, he could not find pleasure in the Buddha-dharma.
Therefore, even though a practitioner possesses the "Exquisite Adornment" as the direct cause, if they do not purify the ālayavijñāna, they will not open the Dharma-eye.

Those who do not possess pure merit are buried and lost; however, since one possesses both the internal primary cause and the external auxiliary conditions, one may enter the Way in the mere twinkling of an eye.
Thereupon, they descend simultaneously to behold the Buddha; at that time, he accords with their capacities to preach the Dharma.
At that time, King Wonderful Adornment and his consort took off from their necks pearl necklaces worth hundreds of thousands and scattered them over the Buddha.
In the midst of the void, they transformed into a precious four-pillared pavilion, within which was a great jeweled couch.
A hundred thousand myriad celestial robes were spread out, upon which a Buddha sat cross-legged, emitting a great radiance.
At that time, King Subhavyūha thought to himself: "The Buddha’s body is rare and extraordinary; it is upright, majestic, and unique, having perfected the foremost and most subtle of forms.
Then, the Buddha Ghanarājasvararājasaṃkusumitābhijña addressed the fourfold assembly, saying: "Do you see this?"
"King Subhavyūha stands before me with palms joined. This king shall become a bhikṣu within my Dharma, diligently practicing and assisting in the dharmas that aid the path to Buddhahood.
He shall attain Buddhahood, named Śālarāja; his land shall be called Mahāprabha, and his kalpa shall be named Mahocchrayarāja.
That Buddha Śālarāja shall have an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas, as well as..."
The measure of the śrāvakas was such that the land was level and upright; its merits were thus.

The king immediately entrusted the kingdom to his younger brother, and together with his queen, two sons, and all his retinue, he left the household life to practice the Way within the Buddha-dharma. Having thus renounced the world, the king—
For eighty-four thousand years, he constantly applied himself with diligent vigor to practicing the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.
After this period had passed, he attained the Samādhi of Adornments of All Pure Merits. He then ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, these two sons of mine have already performed the work of a Buddha; by means of their supernatural transformations, they have converted me."
With their minds set on what is false, they have been enabled to dwell securely within the Buddha-dharma and to behold the World-Honored One.
These two sons are my spiritual friends; wishing to arouse the roots of goodness from past lives and to bring me benefit, they have come to be born in my household.
At that time, the Buddha Cloud-Thunder-Sound-Constellation-King-Flower-Wisdom addressed King Subhavyūha, saying: "So it is, so it is. As...

As for what you have said: "If a son or daughter of good family, by virtue of having planted roots of goodness, obtains virtuous friends (kalyāṇamitra) in life after life—those virtuous friends who are able to perform the work of a Buddha, instructing, teaching, benefiting, and gladdening them, causing them to enter into *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—Great King, you should know that a virtuous friend is a great causal condition (*mahā-pratyaya*). It is for this reason that they transform and guide others, causing them..."
They were able to see the Buddha and resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. "Great King, do you see these two sons?
These two sons have already made offerings to sixty-five hundred thousand million billion *nayuta* of Ganges-sands of Buddhas;
they have drawn near to and honored them, and under those Buddhas, they have upheld the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. Out of compassion for those who are heterodox..."
He saw sentient beings and caused them to abide in right view.
At that time [the phrase] "below" refers to severing attachment to offer it to the Buddha. At the point "in the void," he manifested supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) to increase their faith;

this was according to what the two sons had said. Because they were fond of supernatural powers, he transformed a platform and a Buddha to show them. At that time [the phrase] "below" refers to delight.
Regarding the physical marks of the Buddha’s body: when precious jewels appeared before him, he perceived his own form as defiled.

At that time, clouds descended and he bestowed a prophecy upon the assembly, saying, "If this king becomes a bhikṣu, he shall attain Buddhahood. This was precisely because he wished for the king to renounce his kingdom and leave the household life.
The king accordingly abdicated the throne and entered the monastic order. As a Great Hero who has transcended the world, his courage and resolute intensity were of a singular kind.
Thus it was. When the King went forth from home, he attained the Way; when he spoke thus, he fully realized his former causes and extolled these two words.
This is why he was unaware while intoxicated and only knew them after waking. At this point, King Wonderful Adornment finally met his two sons.
At that time, the Tathāgata certified him, saying: "In the past, you planted roots of goodness."
Because of these roots, he has now attained samādhi and entered bodhi; all of this is due to the power of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
From the words "Great King" onwards, the past lives (*pūrvayoga*) of the two sons are elucidated.
King Wondrous Adornment immediately descended from mid-air and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, the Tathāgata is most rare and marvelous!
By virtue of his merit and wisdom, the fleshly protuberance upon his crown radiates brilliant light; his eyes are long and wide, of a deep azure-blue;
the tuft of hair between his eyebrows is white as a conch or the moon; his teeth are white, even, and closely set, constantly emitting radiance; and his lips—"

The color was a beautiful red, like that of the *bimba* fruit. At that time, King Subhavyūha, having praised the Buddha for such immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of merits, joined his palms with single-minded devotion before the Tathāgata and addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One, it is unprecedented! The Dharma of the Tathāgata is fully endowed with inconceivable, subtle, and wondrous merits;
its teachings and precepts are peaceful, secure, and wholesome. From this day forward, I shall no longer act according to my own whims.”
He did not give rise to any evil thoughts such as wrong views, arrogance, or anger. When these words were spoken, he paid homage to the Buddha and departed.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly: "What do you think? Was the King Subhavyūha anyone else? He is none other than the present Bodhisattva Puṣpadhvaja.
As for his consort, Queen Viśuddhadarśanā, she is the present Bodhisattva Prabhāsa-vyūha-lakṣaṇa before me. Out of compassion..."

It was for the sake of King Wonderful Adornment and his retinue that they were born there. Those two sons are none other than the present-day Bodhisattva Medicine King and the Bodhisattva Superior Medicine.
These Bodhisattvas, Medicine King and Superior Medicine, have accomplished such great merits as these;
having planted the roots of all virtues under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, they have brought them to fulfillment.
Regarding these inconceivable and virtuous merits: if there are those who know the names of these two bodhisattvas, all the devas and people of the world should likewise pay them homage.

When the Buddha preached this "Chapter on the Past Deeds of King Wonderful Adornment," eighty-four thousand people were distanced from dust and freed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.
This is a praise of the Buddha. It says: "Before I had entered the assembly of the Buddhas and had not yet seen the Dharma King, I considered myself supreme and unsurpassed.

But after seeing the Buddha, I realized that the Tathāgata has accomplished immeasurable merit and can further instruct us in the matters we practice in our daily lives, enabling us to attain peace and joy."
Excellent! Having now heard the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, you shall no longer follow the movements of your own mind to practice matters of wrong views or perform acts of wrong views.
Furthermore, you shall not give rise to various forms of self-conceit, arrogance, or anger toward those who are upright.
You are, in fact, none other than the King of Wondrous Adornment; at first you did not believe in the Buddha, but subsequently you desired—
Upon seeing the Buddha, he came to love the Buddha, draw near to the Buddha, and praise the Buddha. For the first time, he realized that all sentient beings have no fixed nature:

if they habituate themselves to evil, they become evil; if they habituate themselves to good, they become good; if they enter into the deviant, they become deviant; if they turn toward the correct, they become correct.

There is ultimately no fixed characteristic; therefore, one knows that when the mind is deluded, it is the *Lotus Sūtra* that revolves [around it], but when the mind awakens, it is the mind that revolves the *Lotus Sūtra*. "The Buddha told...

and below clarifies the distinction between the present and the past. The Bodhisattva Flower Virtue (Huade) is precisely the one who inquires into the original history of Gadgadasvara and who turns the *Lotus Samādhi*.
"The Buddha said... and below concerns the benefits obtained by the great assembly.
The twenty-eighth verse of the Samantabhadra Chapter states:
"I too have devoted my mind to this sutra; I pray, O King, on what day shall we meet in this desolate courtyard?"
If, in the midst of darkness, you permit him to come and touch your crown, first instruct the white elephant to halt beneath the tree.

There are two meanings of Samantabhadra (*Puxian*): "Universal" (*Pu*) refers to pervading the *dharmadhātu*, while "Worthy" (*Xian*) refers to being a sage second only to the Ultimate. This [first meaning] pertains to the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyaksambodhi*), where it belongs to the causal phase.

When referring to the True *Dharmadhātu*, it is called "Universal," and when it encompasses all myriad transformations, it is called "Worthy. This [second meaning] pertains to Sublime Enlightenment (*wushangzhi*).

This pertains to the fruit of attainment. Since this Samantabhadra is the entire substance of the Dharma-realm and the vow-body of Vairocana, after bestowing the prophecy upon the disciple, the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna and all the currently manifesting emanation Buddhas act as witnesses.
Furthermore, following the Bodhisattva’s aspiration to uphold the sutra, the past lives of the Bodhisattva are extensively recounted, and the King of Vows, Samantabhadra, manifests.
Having personally realized it, he exhorted others to resolve their minds upon awakening so that this Dharma might be circulated; thus, this chapter exists.

Now, this sutra cannot establish its fundamental principle without wisdom, nor can it perfect its virtues without practice. It is essential that wisdom and practice advance together, and that virtue and achievement flourish in tandem;
only through such great causal conditions can the matter be brought to fulfillment. Therefore, Mañjuśrī initiates the beginning, while Samantabhadra brings it to completion.
Thus it is said: "To accord with Mañjuśrī’s wondrous wisdom is precisely the original mind;
to enter Samantabhadra’s gate of practice has never been a separate entity."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, by means of his sovereign supernatural powers, majestic virtue, and renown, arrived from the east together with a multitude of great bodhisattvas, immeasurable, boundless, and beyond counting. As they passed through the various lands, all of them were universally shaken.
Rain fell of precious lotus flowers, and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of various kinds of music were played.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
Surrounded by a great assembly of humans and non-humans, each manifesting their majestic power and supernatural faculties, they arrived at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the Sahā world.
There, they prostrated with their heads at the feet of Śākyamuni Buddha, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, from the land of the Buddha Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja, we have heard from afar that this Sahā world is preaching..."
The Lotus Sutra. Together with immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of bodhisattvas, they have come to hear and receive it.
We pray that the World-Honored One will explain it for them. If there are good sons or good daughters who, after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata...
"How can one obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*? The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra:

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family accomplishes four dharmas, they shall obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata. First, they are protected and remembered by all Buddhas;
second, they plant the roots of all virtues; third, they enter the assembly of those fixed in right determination (*samyaktvaniyāma*); fourth, they resolve to save even a single [being]."

It accords with the hearts of all sentient beings. Sons and daughters of good family, if they thus accomplish these four dharmas, they will certainly obtain this sutra after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata.
First, Samantabhadra sets out; he is swift without hurrying and arrives without traveling. Thus it is called "sovereign spiritual power.
It gives rise to reverent contemplation in people and inspires faith in them; thus it is called "majestic virtue. Possessing this majestic virtue, one is virtuous wherever one stands;
therefore, his name is heard everywhere. As for his coming from the east, when the time comes to expound the sutra, a single ray of light...
When he gathers his emanations, one ray of light shines toward the east; when he summons the Bodhisattvas, one ray of light shines toward the east;

therefore, the Bodhisattvas also come from the eastern direction. Because the myriad practices of Samantabhadra are fundamentally not separate from daily activities and deeds, all the lands through which [the light] passes tremble. This is simply because of non-action; were there action, then all things would arise.
Because they were struck with awe. As for the raining of flowers and the playing of music, it was to repay their past causes.

As for the eight classes of beings each manifesting supernatural powers, it was because they had all attained the Samādhi of the Pores of Samantabhadra. From the words "addressed the Buddha" onwards, they personally explained the purpose of their coming.

Regarding the name of the Buddha, "Jewel Splendor Supreme Sovereign" (*Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja*): he is the most majestic, most honored, and most noble sovereign above all, and is therefore called thus.

"Treasure," and he is also called the "Supreme King. This means that because he has heard from afar that the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* is being preached in this land, he has come to hear and receive it.
As for "hearing from afar," it refers to the mental hearing that penetrates the ten directions. How can one obtain this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*?
Regarding "obtaining," it specifically means that even in states of exile, hardship, distress, or sudden calamity, one never loses this [sūtra].
This is a single fascicle of a great sūtra. From the words "If one is skillful" (*yadi kuśala*) onwards, [the Buddha] instructs on the method for obtaining this sūtra.

Regarding the phrase "protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas": this sūtra is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas; therefore, those who can protect and mindfully uphold this sūtra shall also be protected and mindfully upheld by all Buddhas.

Regarding the phrase "planting the roots of all virtues": there is nothing among the six perfections (*ṣaṭ-pāramitā*), the ten powers (*daśa-bala*), the four fearlessnesses (*catvāri vaiśāradyāni*), and so forth, that is not planted.
Furthermore, as for entering the stage of right determination (*samyaktva-niyāma*), there is no samādhi—such as the *Sukusuma* or *Sudhvaja*—that one does not enter.
As for giving rise to the mind that seeks to save all sentient beings, there is no being among the twelve classes of birth who is not delivered.
If one accomplishes these four dharmas, one will certainly obtain this sutra, just as Bhaiṣajyarāja obtained it and then burned his body, and as Gadgadasvara did.
By attaining this, Mañjuśrī transformed his seat; Avalokiteśvara attained this to respond universally; Miaozhuangyan attained this to turn away from evil;
and Samantabhadra attained this to recite mantras and so forth. Question: Are these four dharmas identical to or distinct from the four practices of peaceful bliss (*catur-āśvāsa-carita*)?
Answer: The four practices of peaceful bliss refer to the method for preaching the sutra; these four dharmas refer to the method for upholding the sutra.
Nevertheless, these are all virtues that benefit both oneself and others; thus, they are both identical and distinct.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, in the final five hundred years, during this age of turbidity and evil..."
To those who receive and uphold this sutra, I shall provide protection;

I shall eliminate their manifest afflictions and cause them to attain peace and security, ensuring that no one seeks to find an opportunity to harm them—whether it be Māras, sons of Māra, daughters of Māra, subjects of Māra, or those possessed by Māra; or whether they be yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, or...
Whether it be *kumbhāṇḍas*, *pūtanas*, *vetālas*, or any other beings who cause distress to people, none shall find an opportunity to harm them.

Whether this person is walking or standing, if they recite this sutra, I at that time shall mount the six-tusked white elephant king and, together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas, go to their location, manifest my own form, provide offerings and protection, and comfort their minds. Furthermore—
For the sake of making offerings to the Lotus Sūtra, if this person sits and contemplates this sūtra, at that time I shall again mount the king of white elephants and appear before that person.

If there is even a single phrase or a single verse of the Lotus Sūtra that this person has forgotten, I shall instruct them in it and recite it together with them, restoring their mastery of it. At that time, they shall uphold, receive, read, and recite it.
Regarding the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*: those who behold my body will experience great joy and become even more diligent.

Because they have seen me, they immediately attain samādhi and dhāraṇīs, such as the *Vartanī-dhāraṇī*, the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *Vartanī-dhāraṇīs*, and the *Dharmasvara-upāya-dhāraṇī*. Having attained such dhāraṇīs as these, O World-Honored One, if later...
“World-Honored One, in the final five hundred years, during this age of turbidity and evil, if bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
and upāsikās— those who seek it, uphold it, read and recite it, or transcribe it— desire to practice this Lotus Sūtra, they should, for twenty-one days,
cultivate it with single-minded diligence. Once those twenty-one days are complete, I shall mount my six-tusked white elephant...”

Surrounded by himself and immeasurable bodhisattvas, he manifests before that person with a body pleasing to behold for all sentient beings and preaches the Dharma for them, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening them. He also bestows upon them dhāraṇī mantras;
because they have obtained these dhāraṇīs, no non-human being can destroy them, nor shall they be [harmed] by women.
"May they not be deluded. I myself shall also constantly protect these people. I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me leave to recite this dhāraṇī mantra.
Thereupon, he spoke the mantra before the Buddha, saying:
Atandati. Tandapāti. Tandapati. Tandakusale. Tandasetule. Setule. Seturavati. Buddhaparṣaṇi. Sarvadhāraṇyāvartani. Sarvavaśāvartani. Avartani. Saṃghaparivartani.
Kṣaṇi. Saṃghanirghātani. Asaṃkhyeya. Saṃghavagati. Tīre ādye saṃghatulye (ṣa-cha). Arode parode. Sarvasaṃghati-samādhi-garandi. Sarvadharmasuparikṣite. Sarvasattvarūpa-kauśalya-a...
In the land of Śākya, those who uphold the *Sīnāpikṛtideva* shall not be clothed even in a single thread; those who protect it shall not be separated from it by even a single step.

Vetrada—here translated as "a ghost of malevolent incantations"—rides upon a white elephant, which signifies riding upon the power of great vows. Both the white ox and the white elephant are capable of bearing burdens.
Because it enables one to reach far. "Contemplation" means to concentrate the spirit and fix the will to investigate its meaning and intent.

"Cultivation" means to diligently practice and permeate oneself through walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. As the ancient masters said: "A yard of speaking is not as good as a foot of practicing;
a foot of speaking is not as good as an inch of practicing. This is precisely what is meant by "manifesting the body to preach the Dharma."
"Directly facing one another" means presenting [the truth] face-to-face. "Bestowing the dhāraṇī" means handing it over with both hands.
Because the World-Honored One’s Universal Eye (Samantacakṣus) wished to see Samantabhadra but could not find him, he came and addressed the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"You need only give rise to a single thought within the stillness of samādhi, and you will immediately see Samantabhadra. As soon as Universal Eye gave rise to that single thought, he saw him.

Samantabhadra rides upon a six-tusked white elephant in mid-air; whenever one wishes to know the place where sentient beings give rise to thoughts and stir their minds, it is always Samantabhadra manifesting his presence there—it is only that people themselves do not recognize him.
"Bhagavān, if there are bodhisattvas who hear this dhāraṇī, they should know it is the power of Samantabhadra’s supernatural penetrations.

If the Lotus Sūtra circulates in Jambudvīpa and there are those who receive, uphold, and recite it, they should form this thought: 'All of this is due to the majestic spiritual power of Samantabhadra.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, correctly contemplate, and understand its meaning and intent as it has been taught..."
One who practices in this way should be known as one who performs the conduct of Samantabhadra;

having planted deep roots of goodness in the presence of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, they will have their heads stroked by the hands of all Tathāgatas. If one merely copies it down, at the end of that person's life, they shall be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
At that time, eighty-four thousand celestial maidens will perform various musical performances and come to welcome them.
That person will immediately don a crown of the seven treasures and enjoy themselves with pleasure among the court ladies;
how much more so for one who upholds, recites, correctly contemplates, understands the meaning and intent, and practices according to the teaching!

If there is anyone who upholds, recites, and understands the meaning and intent, at the end of that person's life, a thousand Buddhas will extend their hands to them, ensuring they are not terrified and do not fall into the evil realms.

One will immediately go to Tuṣita Heaven, to where the Bodhisattva Maitreya resides. The Bodhisattva Maitreya possesses the thirty-two marks of a great being and is surrounded by a multitude of great bodhisattvas.
There, one will be born amidst hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of celestial maidens as his retinue.
Such are the merits and benefits [of this practice]. Therefore, the wise person should single-mindedly write it out themselves, or [have others write it].
I shall cause others to transcribe it, to receive, uphold, read, and recite it, to maintain right mindfulness of it, and to practice according to its teaching.
World-Honored One, by means of my supernormal powers, I shall now protect this sutra and cause it to be widely disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata.
To ensure that [the lineage] is not severed, the text below clarifies five kinds of Dharma-preachers; these are precisely those who practice the conduct of Samantabhadra.

If one were to consider only the passage below, using the shallow to illustrate the profound, it would suggest that even if one does not practice the other four types but acts as a Dharma-preacher of only one kind—namely, transcribing the scriptures—one will still be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
How much more so for one who practices all five together! "The thousand Buddhas extend their hands" means that they personally assist one with their own hands.

Because one possesses this dharma-gate of great majestic power, one will not be terrified, will not fall into the evil destinies, and will be born in Maitreya’s Inner Court, where one will always be a companion to the various bodhisattvas. Thus, the following concludes [the section].
"You should encourage others to uphold it and cause it to be widely disseminated throughout Jambudvīpa.

This means you must know that wherever in the southern continent of Jambudvīpa there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, transcribe, or make offerings to the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, all such places are due to the spiritual power of Samantabhadra and are the very site of Samantabhadra’s practice; do not entertain thoughts of treating them lightly.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha praised him, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Samantabhadra!
You are able to protect and assist this sutra, bringing peace, happiness, and benefit to many sentient beings. You have already accomplished inconceivable merit."
With profound and great compassion, you have long ago resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and have been able to make such vows of supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) to protect this sutra.
By my own supernatural power, I shall protect those who are able to receive and uphold the name of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Samantabhadra, if there are those who receive and uphold, read and recite, correctly contemplate, and cultivate [this teaching]...
Those who practice the transcription of this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* should be known as having seen Śākyamuni Buddha;
they should be known as having heard this scripture directly from the Buddha’s own mouth; they should be known as having made offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha;
they should be known as being praised by the Buddha with the words "Excellent!"; and they should be known as having had their heads stroked by the hand of Śākyamuni Buddha.
You should know that such a person is covered by the robe of Śākyamuni Buddha. Such a person no longer craves worldly pleasures;
they take no delight in the scriptures or the writings of non-Buddhists, nor do they enjoy associating with those people.
As for those who are evil— whether they are butchers, or those who raise pigs, sheep, chickens, or dogs, or hunters,
or those who trade in female beauty— if such persons are upright in mind, possess right mindfulness, and have the power of merit,
they will not be afflicted by the three poisons, nor will they be afflicted by envy, self-conceit, wrong pride, or overweening pride. Such persons [suffer] little...

One who desires to be content and is able to cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra—Samantabhadra, if after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, during the final five hundred years, there is someone who sees one who receives, maintains, reads, and recites the Lotus Sūtra, that person should form this thought: "This person will, before long..."

One shall proceed to the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), destroy the hosts of Māras, attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turn the wheel of Dharma, beat the drum of Dharma, blow the conch of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma. One shall sit upon the lion Dharma-throne amidst the great assembly of devas and humans.
Samantabhadra, if in a future age there should be those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this sūtra, such persons shall no longer...

If one is greedily attached to clothing, bedding, food, drink, and the necessities of life, yet their aspirations are not in vain, they will likewise obtain the retribution of blessings in this present life.

If there are those who disparage them, saying, "You are but a madman; you practice these deeds in vain and shall ultimately gain nothing," such a person will suffer the karmic retribution of being blind in every lifetime. Conversely, if there are those who make offerings to and praise them...

In this very life, one shall receive the manifest retribution. Furthermore, if one sees someone who upholds this sutra and exposes their faults—whether those faults be real or unreal—that person shall suffer from leprosy in this present life.

If one mocks them with contempt, they shall, in every successive birth, have teeth that are sparse and missing, ugly lips and a flat nose, hands and feet that are twisted and crooked, eyes that are squinted, and a body that emits a foul odor.
Foulness, malignant sores, pus and blood, dropsy, shortness of breath, and all such grave and evil illnesses.
Therefore, Samantabhadra, if you see one who receives and upholds this sutra, you should rise to welcome them from afar, as if honoring a Buddha.

When this "Chapter on Samantabhadra’s Exhortation" was being spoken, bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, immeasurable and boundless in number, attained hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *śītala-dhāraṇīs*.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a trichiliocosm, who were fully endowed with the path of Samantabhadra—
when the Buddha spoke this sutra, the great assembly, including Samantabhadra and the other bodhisattvas, Śāriputra and the other śrāvakas, as well as devas, nāgas, humans, non-humans,
and all others present, were all filled with great joy. They received and upheld the Buddha’s words, prostrated, and departed.

First, he praises his virtue, saying: "You are a Buddha who has already attained realization in the past, yet you are able to manifest supernatural powers and vows within this assembly to protect this sutra.
I, too, shall use my own supernatural power to protect those who receive, uphold, and recite the name of Samantabhadra.
Although this is a mutual expression of praise, in reality, the name of Samantabhadra encompasses an entire section of the scripture.
Therefore, one who upholds the name of Samantabhadra is equal in merit and without distinction to one who upholds the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.
Below the section on Samantabhadra, the benefits of upholding the sutra are praised at length: "One who sees Śākyamuni" means that one who upholds this sutra upholds the body of the Buddha;
"one who makes offerings to Śākyamuni" means that one who upholds this sutra is himself Bhaiṣajyarāja. The Buddha...

"Praising them as 'excellent' means that those who uphold this sutra are beloved by all Buddhas. Stroking their heads with his hand means that those who uphold this sutra have attained the Dharma of the Crown (Uṣṇīṣa).
Being covered by his robes means that those who uphold this sutra are all sent forth by the Tathāgata.
Not craving worldly pleasures means that those who uphold this sutra have already attained the joy of the Dharma. Regarding "not delighting in... [the text continues].
Regarding "external books": because those who uphold this sutra have already attained the unsurpassed treasure of the Dharma; regarding "not associating with such persons":
because the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are their companions; and regarding "evil persons": because they have abandoned evil vows and observances.
One whose mind and intentions are upright is so because they lack a deceitful or crooked mind. One who possesses right mindfulness is so because they lack erroneous deliberation.
"Not being afflicted by the three poisons" and so forth means they are free from the root and secondary afflictions. One with few desires is so because they find worldly flavors thin and insipid.
One who is content is so because they do not pursue external things. "Before long one shall go to the site of enlightenment" means that they will attain Buddhahood.

"Because it is remote. "That which is prayed for shall not be in vain" means that one's wishes are fulfilled according to the mind. "If there should be... and so forth extensively reveals the transgressions incurred by slandering this sutra.
"You are mad," these two phrases express words of contemptuous disparagement. "In this way... and so forth expresses the retribution for such disparagement.

Those who are blind from birth in every lifetime do so because they have destroyed the eye of the True Dharma (*saddharmacakṣus*). Those who suffer from white leprosy do so because they lack the adornment of merit.

"Liaoli" (lao-li) refers to a state of being curled or contorted. "Jiaolai" (jiao-lai) refers to having disoriented pupils. "Foul and filthy" refers to lacking the fragrance of the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*).
"Water-bellies" refers to those whose bellies are empty while their minds are haughty. "Short of breath" refers to a lack of the Great Spirit (*haogqi*).

"Because it is not sufficient. Therefore, the section beginning with "Thus, below" concludes by exhorting [the audience] to accept and uphold [the teaching]. The section beginning with "When this was spoken, below" describes how the great assembly obtained benefit. The section beginning with "The Buddha spoke, below" describes their joyful circulation [of the teaching].
The Great Outline of the Lotus Sutra, Scroll Seven (End)
